quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Driving is:

options.text: Automatically easy.
Very simple.
A complex skill that takes time to learn.
A right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A complex skill that takes time to learn.
questions.explanation: Driving may seem easy once you practice it. But it is actually complex and takes time to master. Driving is a privilege, not a right.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less well your tires grip the road. If you drive too fast, your tires will lose contact with the road and slide on a thin layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but traffic is coming toward you. You should:

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the edge of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn now because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, you can enter the intersection on a green light. Wait in the middle of the intersection for the oncoming traffic to pass before you complete your turn.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle sign is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle sign is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows your reaction time.
Makes you feel less confident.
Gets broken down more quickly by your body.
Decreases driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol in your system slows your reactions, makes you overconfident, and causes you to make more mistakes while driving.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in snow and ice is safe.
Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in snow and ice is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, rain, or in fog. Winter driving is very difficult and requires extra care. Always check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will follow the right-of-way rules.
Wave other drivers forward before you go.
Go through the intersection right away.
Check for other cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for other cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving forward.
questions.explanation: Do not trust traffic signals alone. Other drivers may not follow right-of-way laws. Always check that it is safe before crossing an intersection.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road to use.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over for you.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road to use.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards and road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: When checking your tires, make sure:

options.text: The tread is not worn down.
The air pressure is not too low.
They are not flat.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your tires before driving. Low air pressure or worn tread makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Drivers should use hand-to-hand steering:

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing, using signals, turning on the radio, or using windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
questions.explanation: Use hand-to-hand steering while driving normally at speeds above 15 mph. This is also called push-pull steering.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road:

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or anytime you cannot see objects 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, let traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When can you drive above the speed limit?

options.text: Never.
When no police officer is nearby.
When other cars around you are speeding.
When you are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not speed. Follow the legal speed limit. Driving at safe speeds gives you time to change lanes, slow down, or stop if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: What can help you avoid emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without sudden braking. This prevents the car behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the highest posted speed.
Slow down.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when heavy rain reduces visibility. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is too heavy, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a green arrow and a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. Make sure the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway.
Workers are on or very near the road ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very near the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers are on or near the road. Drive slowly and carefully through this area.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than cars.
They do not need more space to turn than cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay away from these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars do.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park as far off the road as possible and wait.
Use hand signals to show what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers, take your turn, and go through carefully.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three

questions.correctAnswerText: All three
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot stop you from getting impaired.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when you see warning signals. Do not try to go around a lowered gate. Warning signs include red flashing lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train sounds.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they're yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: The driver on the right has the right-of-way. Let them go first. You can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a green light that has been on for a long time?

options.text: Get ready for it to turn yellow.
Speed up to go through before it turns red.
Assume the light will stay green.
Assume the light is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready for it to turn yellow.
questions.explanation: If a green light has been on for a while, it may soon turn yellow or red. Start slowing down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on quickly.
Release the gas, slow down, then gently steer back on when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas, slow down, then gently steer back on when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Release the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back on with a small turn of the wheel. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on hazard lights.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Slow down and enter the roundabout carefully. Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way at which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop. This gives you the right-of-way to turn left.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down and watch carefully. Be ready to stop.

questions.question: Where are solid white stop lines painted across traffic lanes?

options.text: In curves and on hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines at intersections and crosswalks. They show where you must stop before proceeding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds. This sign warns you that wet roads are slippery and hard to control. Drive carefully and slowly.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.
Replace tires with bad tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose grip and slide on water. This happens with low air pressure, worn tread, and high speed on wet roads. Do all three things to stay safe.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign in a line of cars. The cars ahead have passed through. What must you do?

options.text: You may proceed through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car directly ahead of you without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Always make a complete stop at a stop sign. Check for traffic before proceeding. Do not follow other cars through without stopping.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward left on a barricade mean?

options.text: The driver should stop.
The driver should bear to the right.
The driver should bear to the left.
The driver should drive in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should bear to the left.
questions.explanation: Stripes on a barricade guide your direction. Stripes sloping down and to the left tell you to go left. Stripes sloping down and to the right tell you to go right.

questions.question: What should you do when a car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right if there is an open lane.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you, move right if possible. If you cannot move right, slow down gradually when it is safe to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the danger of being hit from behind.
